headline: Graph and contrastive models integrate spatial, single-cell and histology omics data
label: Multimodal Omics Integration Methods
summary: Spatial, single-cell and histology datasets often have partial or mosaic modality coverage, motivating integration methods that address it directly.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned integration of heterogeneous omics and imaging modalities using architectures that encode structural priors. Graph neural networks recur: CMGL estimates per-patient modality confidence via evidential deep learning before classifying cancer subtypes on a consensus patient-neighborhood graph, SpaMosaic combines contrastive learning and graph neural networks for mosaic spatial multi-omics integration, and INSPIRE uses adversarial graph neural networks with NMF across spatial transcriptomics datasets. Other items instead predict molecular profiles from histology, including H2O and EP-Booster, while scFNSA factorizes modality-specific variational representations. What is new is explicit handling of modality uncertainty, partial or mosaic coverage, and cross-modal inference from H&E, though designs and scope differ across items rather than sharing one approach.
